Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and lots of helpful context on your semantic search requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: Improve Product Search relevance for long-tail queries across 30k SKUs (current infra shows degradation for queries with synonyms and abbreviations).
- Success metrics you care about: Recall@10, MRR, and percent of queries improved vs baseline (current baseline: Recall@10 ~0.62 on a small holdout).
- Constraints: 99ms median token latency target for the overall search path; cost sensitivity where cheaper embedding options are preferable if quality is comparable.

What we’ll do next (plan):
1) You share a small sample (2k queries + labeled canonical results) — thanks for the export you mentioned.
2) We’ll run an initial fit evaluation across 2–3 embeddings variants (recommended below) and return a short report with Recall@k/MRR and per-segment breakdowns (long-tail / synonyms / short queries).
3) If we see regressions, we’ll iterate on prompt sets and consider dimensionality/quantization tradeoffs.
4) Schedule a 45min model-fit review with your team where Marcus and Marissa will walk through results.

Initial recommended candidates (for evaluation):
- redwood-emb-large-v1 (1536 dims) — higher-capacity, best for synonyms/semantic nuance
- redwood-emb-small-v1 (768 dims) — lower-cost, good baseline to check cost/quality tradeoff
- text-embedding-3-small (third-party baseline) — to compare against an external baseline

Attachments: I’ve attached the prompt_set_v1.csv we discussed (simple query normalization + augmentation). Please also attach the sample dataset when you’re ready.

Next meetings: Marcus suggested Wed 2026-08-12 or Thu 2026-08-13 for the review. I’ve tentatively proposed Thu 13 at 16:00 PT on the calendar invite link below — please let me know what works.

Thanks — we’ll treat the first run as a quick validation (24–48h turnaround once we have the sample).

Cheers,

Hi all —

I ran a quick pass on Sara’s sample (thanks!) to get a sense of signal. Below are preliminary notes — these are exploratory, not the full evaluation we’ll produce after the full run.

Preliminary eval summary (sample, ~2k queries):
- Models run: redwood-emb-large-v1 (1536d), redwood-emb-small-v1 (768d), text-embedding-3-small (1024d baseline)
- Metrics (approx):
  - redwood-emb-large-v1: Recall@10 = 0.78, MRR = 0.62, median cosine(sim) within true positives = 0.71
  - redwood-emb-small-v1: Recall@10 = 0.72, MRR = 0.56
  - text-embedding-3-small: Recall@10 = 0.70, MRR = 0.54
- Observations: large model improves long-tail synonym cases (SKU synonyms, model numbers) noticeably; small model is competitive on head queries but drops on synonyms and abbreviation expansion.

Drift and dimensionality considerations:
- Dimensionality impacts storage and retrieval latency: 1536 dims incurs ~1.8x storage vs 768 dims; latency difference is modest with our ANN index (approx +10–15ms median).
- We observed a small cluster drift for product descriptions updated in the last 7 days — recommend adding a freshness-aware weighting during rerank or more frequent re-embedding of changed SKUs.

Next technical steps I recommend:
1) Full evaluation run (24–48h) across the 2k sample with per-segment metrics (synonyms / abbreviations / long-tail).
2) A/B test plan: float32 large vs quantized 8-bit large to measure quality vs cost tradeoffs (we’ll compute unit-cost estimates for 1M queries/month).
3) Expand prompt_set_v1 with targeted augmentations for known synonym patterns (I attached an initial eval report).

I attached a short PDF with the exploratory charts and nearest-neighbor failure examples to illustrate the regressions and wins. Will walk through these in the call on Thu.

Regards,
Marcus
